source.title: Concept Acupuncturist: An Efficient and Precise Concept Erasure Method for Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Yi-Ran Xiahou; Si-Liang Qin; Kai Chen; Sheng-Zhi Zhang; Renyang Liu

record.file_problem: The text contains the paper and appendix; no material garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a different method from Toy Models of Superposition, but reports results on whether SAE features in diffusion models correspond to meaningful concepts and remain consistent across related backbones.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and discusses neuron polysemanticity, but does not test toy-model superposition, capacity pressure, or LLM representations. Rows cover its explicit SAE-feature interventions and the cross-backbone feature comparison in Table X. Output-level unlearning scores and Table IV FO/FAC comparisons are omitted: they evaluate unlearning methods, not whether SAE features are complete or canonical representation units.
record.test_reason: This is a concept-unlearning method paper. It uses pretrained SAEs (from Surkov et al.) as a tool to localize and suppress concept features in diffusion U-Nets, and it reports its own method's forgetting, quality, robustness and efficiency. Table X lists the feature IDs its selection algorithm picked on SDXL-Turbo and SDXL, using the same shared SAE. It does not assess whether SAE features are complete, canonical or stable units: the SAE itself is fixed across the two models. Fig. 4 is a qualitative preliminary motivating the method. Cross-model SAE transfer is cited from [33], not tested here.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly off. The authors' main conclusion is that ConceptACP, which internalizes SAE-feature corrections into a single fine-tuned cross-attention block, beats state-of-the-art baselines at forgetting while keeping image quality and cutting fine-tuning cost. Concept-dependent feature dispersion and the cross-backbone feature differences are secondary discussion points in §VII and Appendix D.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies SAE feature localization and concept removal in diffusion models; it does not reproduce the toy-network setup or measurements of Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature lists and cross-backbone consistency vary by concept; VanGogh differs more across SDXL-Turbo and SDXL than Nudity, Church, or Parachute.

fits_no_version.finding: Using one shared SAE, the concept features the method selects largely coincide between SDXL and SDXL-Turbo for Nudity, Church and Parachute (e.g., 6 of 8 Church IDs shared). VanGogh shares only one ID.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A distilled diffusion model activates largely the same SAE features for a concept as its base model, with concept-dependent exceptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Suppressing feature #4913 removes nudity, but no single one of the top-5 Church features removes Church. Object concepts map to more, more dispersed SAE features than attribute concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concepts vary in how many SAE features they map onto; object concepts are spread over several features.

record.problems: The cross-backbone feature comparison covers four concepts and two related diffusion backbones. Figure 4 reports qualitative interventions without quantitative rates or stated uncertainty. The paper does not establish completeness or canonical status of the SAE features.
record.rows_left_out: Table IV FO/FAC scores and the remaining unlearning effectiveness, quality, robustness, efficiency, and hyperparameter results were left out because they evaluate unlearning performance or costs rather than SAE-feature completeness or stability as representational units.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity-dimension transition or geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity is cited (Toy Models, Zoom In) as motivation only; no capacity test.
No LLM study. Diffusion-model SAEs are used, not tested as evidence of superposition.
Completeness, stability across SAE training runs or sizes, and canonicity are not tested. SAE transfer across SDXL and SDXL-Turbo is cited from [33].
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (tests, T2) and its V5 labels are overturned. The paper relies on SAE features as a tool, and the Table X rows are its own algorithm's selection outputs under a shared SAE. Rows are relinked to none, and the findings are moved to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test toy networks, feature sparsity versus dimensionality, or superposition geometry.
The paper discusses neuron polysemanticity but does not test whether it results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
No test of whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study is about diffusion models, not LLMs, and does not test feature spread across neurons in LLMs.

Tests selected SAE features' concept relevance and some cross-backbone consistency, but not whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable across prompts, training stages, and broader model families.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features or other representational geometries.
